A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianOcc and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. v3 Sections 6–8 correspond to v4 Appendices A–C, allowing reliable comparison across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original GaussianOcc occupancy and depth results on nuScenes and DDAD, together with ablations, rendering-time measurements and pretraining experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a learnable-scale ablation and rendering-time measurements across voxel resolutions.

M1.justification: v4 introduces a tested learnable Gaussian-scale variant using a sigmoid and maximum scale of 0.12 for depth rendering (Table 5); v3 tests fixed scales only. The two-stage GSP/GSV pipeline remains, and semantic occupancy rendering still uses fixed scales.

E1.justification: Both versions cover nuScenes/Occ3D and DDAD surround-view depth and occupancy estimation, plus self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised Occ3D finetuning. Removing the supplementary DDAD montage does not remove DDAD evaluation, which remains elsewhere.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 5 illustrates GaussianOcc alone; v4 Figure 5 explicitly compares it with direct bilinear cross-view synthesis from SurroundDepth. Comparator membership in the numerical benchmark tables is unchanged. GaussTR and VisionPAD are newly cited, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds rendering-time comparisons at fixed 180×320 image resolution across 16×200×200, 24×300×300 and 32×512×512 voxel grids (Table 8), and evaluates learnable scales under the retained ground-truth-pose control (Table 5). Section 3.3 also revises the stated grid from 320×320×24 to 300×300×24; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 extends the scale ablation with a learnable variant, adds sensitivity of rendering time to Gaussian count, and introduces a visual analysis of bilinear-projection failure. Figure 7 pairs the already reported one-stage failure with its overlap mask; it does not establish a new one-stage experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Point estimates, approximate runtimes and averaging across views or epochs remain the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results are unchanged. Table 5 adds learnable-scale results: Abs Rel 0.212, Sq Rel 3.248, RMSE 7.112 and threshold accuracy 0.771. New Table 8 reports VR times of approximately 0.50/0.85/1.52 seconds versus SR times of 0.06/0.17/0.44 seconds across its voxel settings. Qualitative comparisons are revised, and the extra DDAD montage is removed.

T1.justification: Equation (3) changes the formal stage-two loss statement from an unweighted sum to Ltemporal + λLsemantic, with λ = 0.02. This is a limited revision of the stated mathematical objective, without establishing an implementation change. The projection equation and depth-metric definitions remain unchanged; no new proofs or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The headline contributions and 2.7-times training/5-times rendering claims remain. The conclusion drops its explicit assertion of strong generalization to surround-view scenes. The pretraining benefit remains in Appendix B and Table 11, so that contribution is relocated rather than removed.

C2.justification: v4 attributes the semantic-depth discrepancy to OccNeRF's 25% semantic sampling, explains sky-depth artifacts and bilinear-projection failures, and identifies Gaussian count as the principal rendering-time factor. It removes the explicit two-stage training-cost caveat and proposed future one-stage training, while retaining discussion of one-stage failure.

D1.justification: v4 specifies the semantic weight, learnable-scale cap, stage-one depth resolution of 224×352 and Gaussian counts, and adds a pointer to sampling code. It omits v3's 600/150 scene counts, occupancy bounds and 0.4m voxel size, and explicit DDAD spatial bounds. These omissions do not demonstrate changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: v4 adds GaussTR to the Gaussian-splatting related work and cites VisionPAD in the introduction. It also explicitly distinguishes RenderOcc's ground-truth 2D supervision from self-supervision. The broader positioning against volume rendering and earlier Gaussian methods remains.

P1.justification: v4 edits the abstract, introduction and method explanations, clarifies ego-pose terminology, shortens the conclusion and adds acknowledgments. Supplementary sections become Appendices A–C, and the pretraining discussion moves there. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The visual exposition is substantially reworked: Figure 2 becomes a color-coded pipeline diagram, Figure 5 becomes a comparative display, and Figures 6–7 revise the rendering and one-stage illustrations. Figure 4 gains annotations, Table 5 expands, and a new timing Table 8 appears. The DDAD montage and redundant main-text pretraining table disappear, while their retained counterparts are matched across relocation.

improvement.justification: The learnable-scale test, Gaussian-count timing analysis, clearer pipeline diagram and explicit parameters provide a limited improvement in validation and explanation. Benefits are tempered by omitted dataset details and inconsistent RenderOcc supervision labels: v4 Table 1 changes the label, but Tables 9–10 retain the old one. The principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
